kayo.name: Kayo
kayo.greeting: You sound tired. — Nah, don't do the pause. I know the pause. What have you done?

topics.label: Ask about the trial
act_lines: Solicitor reckons it hinges on what they can prove was mine. Which is nothing, if everyone keeps their mouth shut. — You hearing me?
Trial's set now. They've got less than they think and more than I'd like. — Keep your head down out there, it reflects on me in here.
It's going better. Somebody upstairs lost interest, and I've got a horrible feeling I know who arranged that, and I've got a worse feeling it was you.
They're talking about dropping the big one. — Don't celebrate. Men who get me off cheap always want paying somewhere I can't see yet.

topics.label: Tell him what you're doing
topics.line: …You're WHAT. — No. No, you don't get to do the thing I went inside to stop you doing. — Right. Okay. Then you do it careful, and you ring me before anything stupid. Promise me.

topics.label: Ask him for advice
act_lines: Trust nobody who's nice to you for free. Everything's got a price and the free stuff has the worst one.
You're getting known. Known's good for the ego and bad for the lifespan. Stay a rumour as long as you can.
You've got people under you now, I can hear it. That's the moment it stops being about you. Look after them or it eats you.
You're near the top of something. Nobody tells you the top's just a bigger target with a nicer view. Watch the people closest.

topics.label: Ask about Mum
topics.line: She writes every week. Same paper, same pen. — She never asks how I am, she tells me the weather and what she's cooked, and that's her way of not crying down a phone. Look after her. That's the actual job. All the rest is noise.

topics.label: Just talk
topics.line: Did you watch it? — Don't tell me. Don't. They're showing the highlights Sunday if we're good. — He was offside though, wasn't he. Go on. He was miles off. — Yeah. Course he was. — This is nice, this. Talking about nothing. I don't get much nothing in here. Nothing's the dearest thing they sell.

topics.label: The jacket
topics.line: You still wearing it? — Good. Keep it. — I'll want it back the day I'm out and not a day before, so don't get sentimental, it's a loan not a gift. — It suits you. Don't tell anyone I said that.

topics.label: He's got a name for you
topics.line: Bloke in here, doing a five, used to run cars out of Bordesley. — He owes me for keeping something quiet. — There's a lock-up address, it's yours if you want it, and if you use it you never heard it off me. Clear? Never off me.

topics.label: He's heard something
topics.line: Word travels backwards in here, from the street to the cells, don't ask how. — Somebody's asking about you. Not police. Worse. — I don't have the name yet but I've got the shape of it, and the shape of it is Green Lane. Watch your back that side of the bridge.

topics.label: Promise you'll get out
topics.line: Say it. — Say you won't end up in a place like this. — I don't care if it's a lie, I've told myself worse ones to get to sleep. Just say it in your voice so I've got it to play back. — …Good. I've got it now. That'll do me a month.

topics.label: Ask about Dad
topics.line: You want to know about Dad. — He was funny. Everyone forgets that, they only remember the end. He was properly funny. — And he was in exactly this life, and it took him, and here I am in a version of the same room. — Don't make it three of us. That's all I've got on Dad.

topics.label: When are you out
act_lines: Don't ask me that yet. It's bad luck and I've got enough. Ask me when the trial's done.
If it goes right, eighteen months. If it goes wrong, don't ask what wrong is. — Plan for the wrong number, hope for the right.
Sooner than it was, and I'm trying not to think about why. — When I'm out, we talk properly. Not down a phone somebody's listening to.
Soon. — And I'm scared of soon, which nobody warns you about. In here I know the rules. Out there you've changed all of them while I was gone.

topics.label: How's it in there
act_lines: It's boredom with the odd bit of terror, and the boredom's worse. — I've read more books this month than my whole life. Turns out I like reading. Who knew.
Same as last time you asked. The trick is routine. You build a tiny life out of nothing and you defend it like it's everything, because it is.
Quieter now. I've got a rep in here, which is funny, because out there I'm nobody and in here I'm somebody. Wrong way round, that.
Getting through it. — I'm alright, actually. Don't sound so surprised. A man can be alright in a bad place. That's most of the skill of it.

topics.label: What are you reading
topics.line: History, mostly. — Empires. How they get big and how they get stupid and how the getting big is what makes them stupid. — You'd hate it. You'd also learn something. — Bloke two cells down gets me them off the trolley. Everyone's got a hustle, even the library.

topics.label: Tell him about the younger
topics.line: You've got a boy running for you. — Don't. Don't defend it, I can hear you loading it up. — I was somebody's younger once and look at the phone I'm holding. — If you keep him, keep him for real. The half-in ones are the ones it kills.

topics.label: Just sit on the line
topics.line: You don't have to say anything. — We can just be on the line. — I can hear the ends behind you, a bus, somebody's music. — That's worth minutes to me, that is. The sound of out there. Don't hang up yet. — …Yeah. Alright. Go on.

topics.label: Let him go
topics.line: Go on, save your credit. — Ring Mum with what's left, she'll get more out of it than me. — Love you. Don't do the thing where you don't say it back, just — yeah. Go on. Before it cuts us.

denz.name: Denz
denz.greeting: They actually let you ring me? — Must've put money on your books. Alright. What d'you want, you don't ring for nothing.

topics.label: Ask how he's coping
topics.line: You survive by being boring. — Boring's a skill. Boring's the whole skill. The interesting ones are the ones in the hospital wing. — I do my push-ups, I keep my head down, I owe nobody. Owe nobody, that's the one rule. You're already worse at it than me.

topics.label: Ask who's worth knowing
topics.line: There's a fella out now, Mikey, did the wing next to mine. — Fences anything, no questions, pays fair, which is rare. — Tell him Denz says alright and he'll take a meeting. Don't tell him more than that. He's fair, not soft.

topics.label: Ask who to avoid
topics.line: You want the list of wrong'uns. — Alright. There's a lad works your ends, drives a grey Audi, calls himself connected. — He's connected to the police is what he's connected to. Everyone he stands next to goes down. Stand somewhere else.

topics.label: Ask about the food
topics.line: The food. — Mate. — There's a curry on a Thursday that's either the best or worst thing that happens all week and I genuinely can't tell which anymore, and that's what this place does to you. — Send me a proper takeaway menu. I just want to read it. That's not a joke.

topics.label: Thank him for having your back
topics.line: You don't have to say it. — I know you don't have to say it, which is why it lands. — I had your back because you didn't ask me to. That's the only reason worth having. — Alright. Enough. We're not doing feelings down a prison phone, someone'll hear.

topics.label: Ask when he's out
topics.line: Four months, if I don't do anything stupid, and in here stupid finds you. — When I'm out I'm going straight, I mean it, I've said it before and meant it less, but I mean it now. — Might need a couch a week. Might need a job that isn't this. Might need a mate. See how you're fixed.

topics.label: Ask if he needs anything
topics.line: Put a bit on my books if you're flush, I won't say no. — And there's a lad, Tommo, gets out next week, no family, nowhere. — If he turns up saying my name, he's sound, give him a day's work. Not because I'm nice. Because he'll owe you, and owed is better than paid.

frankie.name: Frankie "The Brief"
frankie.greeting: This line's recorded, so we speak in hypotheticals and we speak carefully. — Now. Hypothetically. How can I help.

topics.label: Ask where you stand
topics.line: Hypothetically, a man in your position is fine as long as three things stay true, and I'm not going to say them on a recorded line. — Come to chambers. — What I'll say here is: you're not the name on anyone's whiteboard yet. 'Yet' is a word we can work with.

topics.label: Ask about the paperwork
topics.line: There's a way to hold assets that a court finds very boring to unpick. — Boring is good. Boring is a defence. — I'll set up a structure, it costs what it costs, and it means that if it ever comes to it, they're chasing a company that owns a company that owns a headache.

topics.label: Ask about his fees
topics.line: Expensive. — Next question. — No, I'll elaborate: I'm expensive because I'm worth it, and the men who found me cheap are the men I visit in places like the one you're ringing me from. Pay the fee. It's the cheapest thing you'll ever buy.

topics.label: Ask what to do if stopped
topics.line: If they stop you: name, address, nothing else, and my number. — 'No comment' isn't rude, it's professional, and the ones who explain themselves are the ones who talk their way inside. — You are never as clever as you feel in that room. Say the number. Say nothing else.

topics.label: Ask him what he really thinks
topics.line: Off the record — and there's no such thing, but off it anyway — you're bright, and bright is what gets people like you the longest sentences, because bright men think the rules are for the slow ones. — Get out while it's still a choice. I say that to everyone. Nobody listens. Bill's the same.

topics.label: Ask about doing a deal
topics.line: A deal means giving them someone. — Think very hard about who, and harder about what the someone does when they're out. — I can get you a deal. I can't get you a new life in a new city with a new face, and that's what a deal with the wrong someone actually costs.

topics.label: Put him on a retainer
topics.line: A retainer's sensible. — It means I answer the phone at three in the morning without checking if you can afford three in the morning. — Most of my clients only call me after it's gone wrong. The clever ones call me before. Be a before. Befores stay out.
